text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000201 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity tier, but the few returned charts support the billed levels, so the pattern cannot yet be called upcoding or a legitimately complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not explained by panel mix. The provider's 99215 share exceeds the all-provider rate in every condition-count band, and it is most pronounced among patients with one chronic condition. Sampled examples such as C0099067 (age 18, type 2 diabetes only) and C0099148 (no chronic conditions, urinary tract infection code) are the kind of low-complexity 99215 visits that warrant scrutiny. On the other side, none of the returned documented claims at any level fell below the billed level. The 99215 notes, including low-complexity claim C0099099, recorded high MDM. Every note claiming moderate-or-higher data review had a matching lab or test line, so there is no sign of cloned documentation. With only 5 documented 99215 claims, the documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with C0099067, C0099148, C0099102 and C0099162. The reviewer should then check whether those notes show genuinely high-complexity decision-making rather than templated text."}
